styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Maboneng street life, markets and township history.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Apartheid Museum, Constitution Hill and Soweto.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Lion Park, botanical gardens and the Cradle caves.

stays.why: Safest base for first-timers. Gautrain to the airport, malls and restaurants on foot, easy Ubers to the sights.
Gautrain stop, good hotels and the Sunday rooftop market. A calmer, walkable suburb close to the museums.
Downtown arts district with galleries, cafés and street art. Lively by day; take an Uber after dark.
Leafy student neighbourhood with bars and cheap eats on 7th Street. Good value, short drive to town.

food: Try a braai (South African barbecue) and bunny chow, a curry served in a hollowed bread loaf.
Maboneng and Braamfontein have the best café and street-food scene; go at lunchtime and take an Uber back.
Soweto tours often include a lunch stop; ask for a local shisa nyama (grill) spot.
Cheap eats: kota sandwiches, vetkoek and boerewors rolls at markets for around ZAR 40–90.
Book dinner in Sandton or Rosebank. Many kitchens close early; check hours on the day.
more_time: Add a day for Soweto: Vilakazi Street, the Hector Pieterson Museum and a shisa nyama lunch.
History fans can swap a museum for the Cradle of Humankind and Sterkfontein Caves, about an hour's drive.
Add a half-day at the Apartheid Museum and Constitution Hill if you have a third day.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the Apartheid Museum, Maboneng and a Soweto half-day; add a night for the Cradle of Humankind.

month_notes: January: warm and wet, about 14 rain days. Pack a rain jacket and plan indoor sights.
February: similar to January, warm with frequent afternoon showers.
March: warm with fewer rainy days; good for walking tours.
April: mild days around 22°C and cool nights. Comfortable for sightseeing.
May: dry and cool, only about 2 rain days. Bring a warm layer for evenings.
June: cold nights near 4°C and dry. Sunny days but chilly mornings.
July: the driest month, cold nights. Best for clear skies and game drives.
August: dry and cool, warming by day. Good value before spring.
September: warming fast, around 25°C by day. Few rain days.
October: warm and mostly dry; a good shoulder month.
November: warm with more showers returning. Pack a light rain layer.
December: warm and the wettest month, about 16 rain days. Book indoor backups.

climate_guide.summary: High-altitude city with warm, wet summers and dry, cold winters. Rain falls mostly as afternoon thunderstorms.

items.title: Best time: May to September
items.text: Dry, sunny days with few rain days. Cool to cold nights, so pack layers.

items.title: Wet summer (November to February)
items.text: Around 11–16 rain days a month, usually short afternoon storms. Mornings are often clear.

items.title: Cold winter nights
items.text: June and July drop to about 4°C at night. Days stay near 17°C and sunny.

items.title: Mild shoulder months
items.text: April, May, September and October are comfortable, with highs of 20–26°C.

items.title: Afternoon thunderstorms
items.text: Summer storms can be sudden. Avoid open high ground late in the day.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Layers for cool mornings and warm afternoons, a rain jacket in summer, and a warm jacket for winter nights.

transit.best: Uber or Bolt for most trips; Gautrain for the airport and Sandton.

modes.text: Gautrain is the fast, safe rail link between OR Tambo, Sandton, Rosebank and Pretoria.
Metrorail commuter trains are cheap but not advised for tourists.
City and Putco buses are limited; minibus taxis are cheap but risky for visitors.
Uber and Bolt work well; use comfort or black options where possible.
Renting a car gives the most flexibility; traffic peaks 06:30-09:00 and 15:30-18:30.
Walking is fine in malls and some suburbs; avoid walking between distant areas.
